hero_sub: Everything you need to know to customize your Shizuku-based app's presence on the Shizu CoreFetch Store. Override default GitHub data, configure your developer portfolio, add localized text, and target your custom ads.
what_p1: shizu_store.json is a manifest file that tells the Shizu CoreFetch Android app how to beautifully display your application — overriding the default GitHub data with your custom name, description, icon, developer info, and ads.
what_p2: The Shizu Store automatically discovers and lists Shizuku-based apps. If you don't provide this file, your app will still appear, but it will use your GitHub profile picture as the icon and fetch basic details from your repository description and README. Adding a shizu_store.json unlocks a clean, tailored UI/UX experience for your users.
what_callout: To apply custom branding, the store scans for a file named exactly shizu_store.json at the root of your GitHub repository. The filename is case-sensitive.
place_p1: Place shizu_store.json at the root level of your GitHub repository — the same level as your README.md.
place_p2:
The raw URL to your file will be something like:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<user>/<repo>/main/shizu_store.json
req_p1: If you choose to create a shizu_store.json file for custom branding, it must include these four fields at minimum. If any are missing or invalid, the store will ignore the file and fall back to your default GitHub repository data.
req_desc_pkg: Android package name (e.g. xyz.siwane.myapp). Must be valid Java package format.
req_desc_short: One-line description shown in listings. Max 200 characters.
req_desc_icon: Absolute HTTPS URL to your app's icon. Square PNG or WebP recommended.
opt_p1: These fields enhance how your app appears in the store, including your developer portfolio and community integration.
opt_desc_msg: A personal message to your users displayed in a dedicated card.
opt_desc_ban: Absolute URL to a banner image (16:9 recommended).
opt_desc_scr: Array of absolute URLs to screenshot images.
opt_desc_repo: Direct link to the GitHub repository.
opt_desc_iss: The GitHub Issue number used to fetch and display user comments natively.
opt_desc_ads: Array containing your custom ad configurations (See Monetization section).
opt_desc_dev: Rich developer portfolio info. See below.
opt_desc_loc: Translated strings per language code. See Languages section.
opt_dev_p: The developer object powers the developer dashboard in the store, showing your banner, website, and other apps.
ads_p1: Shizu CoreFetch empowers developers by allowing them to display their own custom ads directly inside their app's details page. You keep 100% of the traffic. Set 'has_ads': true and configure the ads array.
ads_pol_p: Developers have complete freedom to promote their own products, external links, or sponsors. However, the following categories are strictly prohibited: Gambling, Alcohol, Drugs, Pornography, and Religious disparities/paradoxes. Violating this policy will result in the immediate blacklisting of the ad or the application from the store ecosystem.
loc_p1: The Shizu Store natively supports 11 languages. Add translated strings under the locales key using BCP 47 language codes. The store will display the appropriate locale based on the user's device language, falling back to en if unavailable.
loc_callout: You can also add any other language code under locales — the schema allows any BCP 47 code. Additional languages beyond the 11 listed may be displayed if the store adds support later.
loc_trans_p: Each locale object supports these translatable fields:
loc_td_app: App name in the target language
loc_td_dev: Developer's name in target language (e.g. Arabic)
arch_p1: The Shizu CoreFetch store acts as an intelligent bridge. It auto-indexes Shizuku applications and fetches metadata and APK releases directly from the developers' GitHub repositories. There is no direct hosting or intervention from the store itself. The ecosystem relies entirely on the open-source community.
arch_disc_p1: The creator of the Shizu CoreFetch store (Jamal El Hizazi) is not responsible for the functionality, safety, or content of any third-party application published in the store. All responsibility lies solely with the respective app developer.
arch_disc_p2: However, the store administration reserves the absolute right to blacklist or block any application or advertisement if a contradiction with the store's policies is discovered, in order to prevent harm to users.
val_p1: Always validate your shizu_store.json before publishing. Malformed JSON will cause the store to ignore your customizations and display the default GitHub data instead.
val_s3_p: Copy your shizu_store.json into the right (Input JSON) panel and check for errors.
err_1_p: JSON does not allow duplicate keys inside the same object. Most parsers will silently use the last value, which leads to data loss.
err_2_p: JSON does not allow a comma after the last item in an object or array.
err_3_p: All URL fields (icon_url, banner_url, screenshots, etc.) must be absolute HTTPS URLs. Relative paths won't work because the store fetches them remotely.
err_4_p: To apply your custom branding, the file must be named exactly shizu_store.json (lowercase, with underscore) and placed at the root of the repository.
sec_c1_p: The Shizu Store installs APKs silently using Shizuku's elevated system permissions. This is a powerful capability — users who install your app from the store are implicitly trusting you as a developer.
sec_p1: As a developer whose app is listed on the Shizu Store, you agree to act responsibly. This means:
sec_li1: Never serve malware or spyware through your GitHub releases.
sec_li2: Be transparent about what your app does. Accurately describe all Shizuku permissions your app uses.
sec_li3: Publish your source code when possible. Users and reviewers are far more likely to trust open-source apps.
sec_li4: Sign your APKs with a consistent certificate. Never swap a legitimate APK for a malicious one.
sec_li5: Notify users of significant changes via GitHub releases, especially if you are requesting new permissions.
sec_c2_p: Shizuku grants apps ADB-level permissions. Apps running under Shizuku can perform sensitive operations like reading private data, modifying system settings, and managing other apps. Always use the minimum permissions necessary.
faq_1_q: Do I need to submit my app anywhere to be listed?
faq_1_a: No submission is required. The store automatically detects Shizuku-based repositories on GitHub. Adding a shizu_store.json simply gives you full control over how your app is presented to users.
faq_2_q: Can I use a CDN or my own server instead of GitHub raw URLs?
faq_2_a: Yes. Any publicly accessible HTTPS URL is valid for all URL fields. GitHub raw URLs are simply the most common choice because the JSON file lives in your GitHub repo.
faq_3_q: What happens if a user's device language isn't in my locales?
faq_3_a: The store falls back to the root-level (non-localized) values — i.e., whatever you put in app_name, short_description, etc. at the top level of the JSON. We recommend writing those in English.
faq_4_q: Do I have to include all 11 languages?
faq_4_a: No. You can include as many or as few locales as you want. Any locale you omit will automatically fall back to the root-level values.
faq_5_q: How do I format descriptions with bold text and line breaks?
faq_5_a: Use \n for newlines and **text** for bold text within description strings. These are interpreted by the store when rendering the app's detail page.
faq_6_q: My app doesn't require Shizuku to run — can I still list it?
faq_6_a: The store is designed for Shizuku-based apps. You can list it, but be clear in your description that Shizuku is not required for its core functionality.
faq_7_q: Is there a file size limit for the JSON?
faq_7_a: There is no hard limit documented, but keep the file reasonable. A few kilobytes is typical. Avoid embedding very long strings directly — link to external resources instead.
faq_8_q: Can I have multiple apps in the same repository?
faq_8_a: No. Each repository represents a single app in the store's auto-indexing logic. To list multiple apps, create separate repositories for each.
foot_p2: The Shizu Store uses Shizuku for silent APK installation. Developers are responsible for the safety of their apps.
b_header_sub: Smart builder for generating error-free shizu_store.json manifests. Fill the required fields, and expand optional sections as needed.
b_help_scr: Enter one absolute HTTPS URL per line.
b_help_ads: Promote your own links. No gambling, adult, or illegal content.
b_help_loc: Translate your app details. Data is saved automatically when switching languages below.
opt_desc_has_ads: Set to true to enable custom ad banners in your app details. Replaces the deprecated ad field.
opt_desc_cat: App category for store browsing (e.g. 'System Tools').
opt_desc_ver_code: Integer version code used internally by Android.
opt_desc_min_sdk: Minimum Android SDK version required to install the app.
opt_desc_target_sdk: Target Android SDK version the app was built against.
opt_desc_min_shizuku: Minimum Shizuku version code required to run the app.
opt_desc_tags: Array of keyword tags used for search and discovery. Max 15.
opt_desc_download: Absolute URL to the APK file. Must end in .apk.
opt_desc_changelog: Changelog for the current version. Supports \n and Markdown-style formatting.
opt_desc_req_shizuku: Whether the app requires Shizuku to function. Defaults to true.
opt_desc_open_source: Whether the app's source code is publicly available.
opt_desc_donate: Absolute URL to a donation page for the app.
opt_desc_schema_version: Schema version. Must be 1 for the current specification.
loc_td_cat: App category in the target language
b_help_tags: Comma-separated keywords, e.g. shizuku, apk, tools
loc_td_ban: Localized banner image URL for this language
